title-group.article-title: A synthetic erythroid enhancer variant alters GATA1 binding

abstract.p: We tested an invented enhancer variant, rs1427407, in erythroid cells.
The T allele increased GATA1 binding and enhancer activity, whereas the G allele did not.

body.p: Enhancer variants can change transcription factor binding. Here we describe a ﬁctional example with a so­ft hyphen.

sec.title: Binding assays
sec.p:
Electrophoretic mobility shift assays with K562 nuclear extract showed that the T allele probe bound GATA1 more strongly than the G allele probe (Fig. 1).
Figure 1 GATA1 binds the T allele.
EMSA of the T and G probes with K562 nuclear extract.
By contrast, the T and G probes showed no difference in TAL1 binding in the same extracts.

sec.title: Reporter assays
sec.p: In K562 cells, luciferase constructs carrying the T allele gave 2.4‑fold higher activity than constructs carrying the G allele (n = 6; P = 0.003).

sec.title: Genome editing
sec.p: CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of the 300-bp enhancer region in HUDEP-2 cells reduced BCL11A mRNA by 60%.
Base editing that converted the T allele to G in HUDEP-2 cells lowered BCL11A expression by 35%.

sec.title: Chromatin immunoprecipitation
sec.p: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR in heterozygous K562 cells recovered more GATA1-bound fragments from the T allele than from the G allele.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: We propose that GATA1 recruitment to the T allele could explain the “higher” enhancer activity – a hypothesis for later work.

ack.p: We thank the synthetic data team.

sec.title: Online methods
sec.p: K562 and HUDEP-2 cells were cultured under standard erythroid conditions.
